subject.title: [Feature]: Add runtime testing for skill workshop proposals before apply

question: What pre-apply runtime validation boundary should Skill Workshop support for pending proposals?
rationale: The useful load/schema smoke test is clear, but invoking proposed skill behavior before apply can cross approval, sandbox, tool-policy, network, and filesystem side-effect boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Start with load/schema validation
options.body: Add a non-mutating proposal test phase that proves discovery and schema visibility, while deferring representative invocation until a test-case and sandbox contract exists.

options.title: Include opt-in invocation tests
options.body: Allow proposal-provided or maintainer-provided safe inputs and expected outputs, but require explicit side-effect permissions and isolated execution before apply can depend on it.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle-contract design
options.body: Track this under the broader Skill Workshop lifecycle contract work and avoid a standalone test command until the contract authority is settled.

recommendation.title: Start with load/schema validation
recommendation.body: Add a non-mutating proposal test phase that proves discovery and schema visibility, while deferring representative invocation until a test-case and sandbox contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior feature-provenance trail points to shakkernerd as the strongest available owner for Skill Workshop service/API direction.
